Blinken Secretary of State U.S. Department of State 2201 C Street NW Washington, D.C. 20520 Dear Secretary Blinken, On February 6, 2023, a 90-day mass show trial of the 47 democracy advocates began in Hong Kong.' Today marks the second anniversary of the 47 Hong Kong democracy advocates being charged with “Conspiracy to commit subversion” under the Hong Kong National Security Law. At least 150 Hong Kong opposition politicians and activists have been taken into custody on charges related to the Hong Kong National Security Law since the law was enacted in Beijing in June 2020 and more than 1,200 political prisoners are currently detained in Hong Kong.” At this critical juncture, I urge you to call on the Hong Kong Government to end political prosecution on Beijing’s behalf and immediately release all political prisoners. I also request that you take appropriate actions to hold the Hong Kong Government accountable in support of Hong Kong citizens’ fight for freedom. The Hong Kong National Security Law gives the Hong Kong Government the power to arrest, jail and prosecute Hong Kong citizens who stand up to defend their civil and political rights. This law has deprived Hong Kong of judicial independence and is the Chinese Communist Party’s direct assault on the “One Country, Two Systems” principle it pledged to uphold according to the Sino-British Joint Declaration of 1984. Pursuant to the Hong Kong Autonomy Act and Executive Order 13936, the Hong Kong National Security Law has destroyed what remained of Hong Kong’s autonomy.
